title: TypeScript: make invalid states harder to express
outcome: Model request states and narrow outside data instead of hiding uncertainty with any.
useCase: API adapters and reusable Vue components.
benefits: Missing states and unsafe property reads surface earlier.
drawbacks: Types still need runtime validation at outside boundaries.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Types check your claims. Parsers check outside values.

trace.title: Unknown input
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

TypeScript checks code before it runs. It does not validate JSON at runtime.

A cast tells the compiler what you claim; it does not turn a string into a number or verify an API response.

A discriminated union uses one field to distinguish valid shapes. A loading state does not need fake rows and an error at the same time.

Narrow the union before reading a field that exists only in one variant.

Use unknown for data you have not checked. Keep interfaces small at the component boundary.

Prefer a clear union for status to several booleans that allow impossible combinations such as loading=true and finished=true.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
At compile time, narrowing follows kind. At runtime, a parser checks actual values.

Once parsed, UI code can work with the smaller trusted shape. Recheck when a new outside boundary is crossed.

For an exhaustive switch, assign the unreachable value to never. A later added state can then produce a compiler error in code that forgot to handle it.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Non-null assertions hide absence but do not create a DOM element. any spreads unchecked assumptions across the program. Optional properties can conceal a missing required business decision.
